questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The economic cost of climate change
How climate change affects mental health
Why so many young people protest
How to prepare your home for a flood
questions.why: They meet an expert investigating the link between climate change and mental health problems.

questions.q: Who is affected by worry about climate change, according to Rob?
options: Only people who live near the sea
Only scientists who study the climate
Only people who have lived through a disaster
Everyone, not just disaster victims
questions.why: He says it's leading to mental health problems not just for those who experience events first-hand, but for us all.

questions.q: According to the 2021 UK census, how many British adults are worried about climate change?
options: About three quarters
About a quarter
Around half
Almost none
questions.why: Rob says three quarters of adults in Britain are worried about the impact of climate change.

questions.q: What does Dr Gesche Huebner say heatwaves are linked to?
options: Better sleep and more energy
More outdoor exercise in parks
A higher risk of suicide and illness
Fewer natural disasters in summer
questions.why: She says hot temperatures lead to an increased risk of suicide and other adverse mental health effects.

questions.q: What is 'climate anxiety', according to Rob?
options: A serious illness after surviving a flood
A low-level worry about the planet
A strong fear of hot, sunny weather
Anger at governments for doing nothing
questions.why: He describes it as a low-level feeling of nervousness or worry about climate change's consequences.

questions.q: What positive point does Rob make?
options: Climate change is slowing down now
Mental health problems are decreasing
Fighting climate change helps our minds too
Young people are no longer worried
questions.why: He says many things good for fighting climate change are also good for mental health.

questions.q: Which of these does Dr Huebner suggest?
options: Building more roads for cars and lorries
Staying indoors on hot summer days
Moving from the city to the countryside
Changing roads for walking and cycling
questions.why: She says change road infrastructure to enable more walking and cycling.

questions.q: Why does Dr Huebner mention urban greenspaces?
options: Green and blue spaces help mental health
Because they are cheap and easy to build
Because they stop floods in city centres
Because they attract lots of tourists
questions.why: She says 'we already know that green and blue spaces are good for mental health'.
